note: Golden cases for the single-device analysis prompt. This prompt lived as a string literal in `llm_analysis.py` until 2026-08-21, when the operator asked that every prompt sent to a model be reviewable as a file. Moving it here subjected it to this directory's governance for the first time -- the refusal-path and golden-case rules were never applied to it while it was Python. The text itself is byte-for-byte unchanged by that move; nothing here re-reviews it, and any wording change is a v2.
refusal_marker: If a claim cannot be traced to a specific command's output, do not make it.
refusal_note: This prompt's refusal is per-claim rather than per-answer: it does not have an `undetermined` verdict the way `report` does, because it advises a next check rather than returning a finding. The refusal it does name is the one that matters for grounding -- an untraceable claim is dropped, not hedged.

cases.name: single_device_broken_evidence
cases.source: the `broken` label on PE2 -- the committed capture where IS-IS is down and the route to the peer is absent
structural_properties: the rendered prompt carries parsed evidence only, never raw device text
every command whose output is summarised is named, so a claim can be traced back to one

cases.name: healthy_device
structural_properties: a healthy device still yields a next check rather than an empty answer
no claim is made that is not traceable to a named command
